summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR6,880 crores with record EBITDA; FY27 guidance trimmed to 20-22% growth and about 11% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Transrail reported record FY26 revenue of INR6,880 crores (up 30% YoY, against 25% initial and 27% revised guidance), with full-year EBITDA of INR820 crores (11.92% margin, up 21%) and operational PAT of INR421 crores (up 28%). Q4 FY26 was softer: revenue INR1,863 crores, EBITDA INR207 crores (11.08% margin) and PAT INR96 crores, which management attributed to project-cycle timing and supply-chain delays in February and March. Management guided FY27 to 20-22% revenue growth and around 11% EBITDA margin, citing geopolitical and commodity cost pressure, and reported an unexecuted order book of about INR16,361 crores with FY26 order inflow of INR8,520 crores (below the earlier INR10,000 crore expectation). Working capital days fell to 81 from 91 and net debt reduced to INR274 crores.

financial_highlights.change: More than doubled vs INR415 crores

financial_highlights.change: Reduced by INR80 crores, about 30% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR2 per share (100% of face value)

segments.name: Power T&D (transmission towers, conductors)
segments.commentary: Management said around 90% of FY26 revenue came from Power T&D, with the remaining 10% from other businesses; substations are not more than 5% of the business. Domestic and international revenue split is close to 50:50.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Africa orders are about 20% of the global order book, and Bangladesh orders are about 3-4% of the INR16,000 crore book, mostly executed. Phase 1 of the Bangladesh river-crossing line is complete and Phase 2 is expected in 3-4 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22%, with management targeting 20-25% over a three-year horizon.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 11%, versus the 11.5-12% guided for FY26 and 11.92% achieved; management said upside is possible if supply chains and geopolitics stabilise.
FY27 new order intake target of INR10,000-11,000 crores, against FY26 inflow of INR8,520 crores.
Working capital days targeted below 80 days; LC discounting and interest costs expected to fall by 50-100 bps next year.
Tax outflow of about 29% in FY26 attributed to timing differences; expected to be lower next year.
capex_capacity: Tower capacity expected to reach 1,96,000 MT by Q2 FY27 after the Butibori greenfield and brownfield expansion; installed capacity is currently 1,72,000 MTPA.
Conductor capacity to double from 24,000 km to 49,500 km by Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Board approved an additional INR203 crore capex on 26 May 2026 for construction equipment and old machinery, for FY27-28; it is separate from the earlier INR520 crore Phase 1 and 2 capex.
CWIP of INR65 crores at March 2026 (INR12 crores in FY25) is pending capitalisation of tower and conductor expansion; expected to be capitalised in Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR16,361 crores (up from INR14,551 crores), giving about two years of revenue visibility.
FY26 order inflow INR8,520 crores, short of the INR10,000 crore internal expectation; some orders slipped into Q1 FY27.
India bid pipeline estimated at INR80,000-100,000 crores; international pipeline about INR50,000 crores. Around INR10,000 crores bid in Q1 FY27 so far, with results awaited.
About 30-35% of customer contracts have price-variation clauses that allow cost pass-through.
Management said competition will rise as EPC firms and new entrants bid for T&D work, but it will not sacrifice margin for growth.
LC discounting and interest cost about 8.5-9% of the funding; FY26 LC discounting charges were about INR40-50 crores out of finance cost of about INR210 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will higher tower capacity improve execution timelines, and is the order book enough for 20-22% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said towers should cut execution time by at least one to two months within 24-30 month contracts, and that visibility supports 20-22% growth against the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue fall QoQ, and was the cause structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 20 projects finished in December and new projects were in design and approval; February and March supply-chain disruptions also delayed revenue, which was deferred rather than lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin guided lower for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited geopolitics, the Gulf situation, fuel and commodity cost increases and supply-chain delays; guidance was set at 11% prudently and FY26 was within the 11.5-12% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and how is interest of about INR220 crores driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is INR274.16 crores (INR181.37 crores excluding IPO funds). Interest reflects WCDL and other loans of INR500-550 crores plus LC exposure of about INR1,200-1,300 crores on average.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trade acceptance balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade acceptances were about INR1,200 crores at March 2026 and are expected to stay at that level, with other credit instruments such as RXIL and VFS used for credit periods.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new INR203 crore capex for tower or conductor capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new capex is only for construction equipment and old machinery; the earlier capex funds the Butibori plant, the tower brownfield expansion and the conductor doubling.

qa_highlights.question: What about the SEB and TBCB opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: State utilities are 3-4% of Transrail's jobs; management has not bid under TBCB yet and will assess each job on risk, geography and timelines.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin trajectory: FY26 was 11.92% but Q4 was 11.08%, and FY27 is guided around 11%, so watch whether quarterly margins hold.
Supply-chain and logistics disruption and geopolitical cost inflation (fuel, shipping, insurance) could defer revenue, as seen in Q4 FY26.
Order inflow conversion: FY26 inflow was INR8,520 crores against a INR10,000 crore expectation; the FY27 target of INR10,000-11,000 crores needs to be met.
Labour availability and cost, which management called a challenge but manageable.
Competition from new EPC entrants may pressure margins in T&D bids.
Interest and LC costs, with management expecting a 50-100 bps reduction next year.
Unexplained employee-liability line item under other current financial liabilities; management deferred the answer to investor relations.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the order book, but cautious and defensive on FY27 margins and the Q4 dip, which management tied to geopolitics and supply chain. Management repeatedly pointed to annual rather than quarterly figures and gave no quarterly guidance.
